steps: Atomic radius grows down a group and shrinks left to right across a period.
Ionization energy and electronegativity do the opposite: higher toward the top right.
A cation is smaller than its atom. An anion is larger than its atom.
Type the element name, or a ranking like O < S < Se.

worked_example.q: Largest radius: Na, Mg, or Cl?

similar_problem.q: Largest radius: F, Cl, or Br?
similar_problem.hint: They are in one group. Look down.

problems.q: Largest radius: Na, Mg, or Cl?
problems.why: Across a period, more protons pull the cloud in. Na is farthest left.
hints: Bigger atoms sit toward the bottom left. Higher ionization energy sits toward the top right.

problems.q: Largest radius: F, Cl, or Br?
problems.why: Down a group, a new shell makes the atom larger.
hints: Bigger atoms sit toward the bottom left. Higher ionization energy sits toward the top right.

problems.q: Highest ionization energy: Na, Al, or Cl?
problems.why: Ionization energy rises toward the top right. Cl is farthest right.
hints: Bigger atoms sit toward the bottom left. Higher ionization energy sits toward the top right.

problems.q: Highest ionization energy: Li, Na, or K?
problems.why: Ionization energy falls down a group. Li is highest.
hints: Bigger atoms sit toward the bottom left. Higher ionization energy sits toward the top right.

problems.q: Rank by radius, small to large: O, S, Se. Type O < S < Se.
problems.why: Down group 16, the atoms get larger.
hints: Bigger atoms sit toward the bottom left. Higher ionization energy sits toward the top right.

problems.q: Rank by ionization energy, low to high: K, Ca, Br. Type K < Ca < Br.
problems.why: K is lower-left of these three, so it holds its electron most loosely.
hints: Bigger atoms sit toward the bottom left. Higher ionization energy sits toward the top right.

problems.q: Which is larger, the Na atom or Na+? Type sodium atom or sodium ion.
problems.why: Na+ lost the 3s electron, so it lost a shell.
hints: Bigger atoms sit toward the bottom left. Higher ionization energy sits toward the top right.

problems.q: Which is larger, the Cl atom or Cl-? Type chlorine atom or chloride ion.
problems.why: Cl- has one extra electron and more repulsion in the same shell.
hints: Bigger atoms sit toward the bottom left. Higher ionization energy sits toward the top right.

problems.q: Highest electronegativity: N, O, or F?
problems.why: Electronegativity rises toward fluorine, skipping the noble gases.
hints: Bigger atoms sit toward the bottom left. Higher ionization energy sits toward the top right.

problems.q: Lowest ionization energy: Cs, Rb, or Ba?
problems.why: Cs is the farthest down and left of these three.
hints: Bigger atoms sit toward the bottom left. Higher ionization energy sits toward the top right.
